title: divinity: original sin (classic)
text: Innovative, with a look to the past! This game is brilliant, let me start off by saying that. Every aspect of this game shines, like few have recently in this genre. The game is full of nods to the old school era of isometric RPGs (Fallout 1 & 2, Baldur's Gate, Arcanum, Icewind Dale and so on), both in style of gameplay, dialogue and setting, while yet bringing lots of new things by making brave decisions. Let me just say that I have played roughly fifteen hours, and just wandered around doing side-quests, trying to solve a ridiculously intriguing detective-story (so far I've got help from a dog sniffing the suspects pants and snuck into one of the suspects house to read her diary) amongst other things. It is a game full of content and stuff to do everywhere. The story holds up really well so far, but gives plenty of room for going off on other adventures. The UI is great. Slick menus, nice inventory management, lovely character creation. Everything is easy on the eye. Details like these are really important. The combat is great. Turn-based without using grids, the main feature of the combat is the brilliant way it uses elements. My aerothurge-mage conjures a pool of water around my enemies and my archer let's a lightning arrow hit it, ZAP, and they are stunned. Burn water and you get a steamy cloud. Zap it with electricity and you got a static cloud. Put acid on the ground and blow it up with a fireball. I've still not mastered it. You think you are safe but haven't noticed that your characters are all standing in a pool of water, or you think that barrel is just an ordinary one. Lots of classes, easy customizations, nice leveling system with perks and abilities that you can use in different ways. Flare can either be a small fireball on your opponent, or use it on the ground and create a fiery surface that your opponents either will have to walk through and suffer burning damage, or walk around it. The system works great. There is a very good crafting system in place in the game as well. It makes you think logically. In this game you have to pick up and read books with real words (not a fixed schematic) and then drag the items onto each other. Arrowhead and woodshaft, an arrow. A knife and a wood stake? A makeshift spear. There is also alchemy, and lots of reagents to find and pick up everywhere you go. I haven't delved into this part of the game yet, but I intend to. Last but not least, the soundtrack is really great. I've found myself humming the tunes walking around in my apartment, and they complement the game in a great way. It's been a long time since I enjoyed a game (in this genre) as much as this (probably BG2 now that I think of it), and I got lots of it left, thankfully.

title: divinity: original sin (classic)
text: It's been so long since I've had so much fun with a turn based rpg. Of course most of that is due to the fact that there aren't many anymore - unless you count the Japanese ones like Pokemon, which I don't enjoy. So, yes, the combat is fairly simple to get a hang of, but also very challenging. You have to have a strategy to succeed, but you do have the option to flee if things get too hairy. For me, the combat is the best part of the game - which is unusual because I don't normally enjoy combat. I guess it's because each encounter feels unique and because there's a variety of different enemies that require unique strategies to overcome. There are also a bunch of different classes and you can mix and match the skills to make your own blend of character - a fireball throwing thief for example. The magic system is awesome btw. You can light oil on fire, create a rainstorm to put it own, then electrify the water puddles to stun enemies, freeze the water to make them slip etc. Really creates some interesting situations. Mages aren't the only ones who can do this either. Archers can shoot flame, water, poison, ice etc arrows. Something to keep in mind though: this game was made on a tight budget compared to most modern releases. A lot of it of it is voiced, but most of it isn't. It's more like classic RPGs like Bauldur's Gate in terms of dialog. Don't expect Mass Effect cutscenes etc. Also, not a lot of options for character customization. There are some though and I'm sure mods will add more. (Did I mention mods? It comes with the editor the used to make the game and it looks pretty nifty - though I haven't had the chance to play with it much.) The devs might make some additions too. They've been updating it frequently and fixes every little bug that's cropped up. Back to dialog: there are dialog tree and some conversation skills. There's also a conversation mini-game for arguments that I don't enjoy too much, but it's tolerable as it is determined by stats as well as luck. It was probably included to solve disputes when you play multiplayer co-op - which, I haven't played, but most seem to enjoy it. The story is decent - same the universe and all that, but it does seem to be somewhat non-linear - as in it makes room for you to do things in an odd order should you choose. There are a few memorable characters and some unexpected plot twists etc. A lot of content too. The game is actually way longer than I expected. A ton of side quests as well. On the whole you can really tell the devs put their hearts into this and that's a rare thing too these days.

text: A perfect example how to NOT make a game. 2/10 Graphics: Who thought that OpenGL is a good idea for a fast shooter game like this? The over-colored envirements look like extracted from a childs book. textures pop up as you look at them because of that useless "prerender" option that just make the game unplayable at nearly 18fps with a gtx 750 and an i7. (other modern games plays fine with this hardware setup) Leveldesign is pretty okay but not as good as in doom 3. Sound: The soundtrack is great but becomes annoying as hell when you progress in the game. Every time, when enemies spawn, the soundtrack changes to a more agressive combat style until you killed the last enemy from said spawn. This is exactly the same as in painkiller or serious sam but they did it right and doom sadly did not. noises from enemies feel like they are played directly infront of you. I had trouble seeing enemies because the sound indicated a whole other direction than the enemies are actually standing. Gameplay: I had a very bad feeling about the "glory kill" moves at first but they are pretty okay. there are just a few problems with it. first of all, you're not invincible during glory kills.. at least not for the whole kill move wich leads often to death after glory kill animation because you can't move until the animation is fully played. If you try to avoid the glory kills, you often end up shooting more than enough bullets till an enemy gets down without glory kill... I think without the kill moves you need 3 times more bullets then with a glory kill. next thing I'll have to cover is the fact, that this game playes almost exactly like serious sam or painkiller. you enter an area, all doors get locked, a fixed amount of enemies spawn and after you killed them all you can continue to the next area. and with the changig sound, you always know when an enemy is still alive. this ruins the whole scary part that doom3 had. areas with enemies are mostly build in a circle and play like multiplayer maps. enemies spawn in almost every spot at almost the same time so that you end up running in said circles untill every enemy is down. weapon upgrades are just there to make the s*** look a bit better. they're nearly useless in my opinion because the secondary firemode of the weapons do not enough damage to be usefull, I almost never used them. the game offers ingame challanges to unlock some sort of talisman which makes enemies stay longer in the tumbling glory kill state or increases the radius in which items get collected but like the weapon upgrades, they're more or less useless because you just stand right next to the items, when enmies drop them (f.e.) Story and Playtrough: the story feels pretty rushed. you get the chainsaw and I believe the first 4 weapons in the 2nd level of the game. and thats almost everything you need to complete the game (I never used the gatling gun or the bfg which you'll get later) while doom 3 took care of slowly getting into something like a story, the new doom just throws you in hell and then you're back on the mars base and that was it. I knew hardly what I was doing besides clearing areas and walking to the next ones. At certain points you'll have to find a keycard or a switch which is pretty boring depending that this game wants to be an arcade game. I guess they tried to make something like doom 1 but horribly failed. The only good thing is, that the checkpoints are decent placed and there was never a situation where I had no idea what to do next. If you want to play a creepy horror game with some action: play doom 3 if you want to play an arcade game like the good old dooms, just play painkiller or seriouse sam instead. + soundtrack is decent + movement is acceptable + great animations + interesting leveldesign - graphics are too expensive for what they look like - textures are too colorfull imo - glowing "glory kill" effects arround enemies destroy the atmosphere - no quicksave, just checkpoints - enemies look worse than in doom 3 - a lot of useless feautures

text: Underrated masterpiece. The fact it's pretty much the reason Dead Space exists is reason alone to respect this game to an obscene degree. Doom 3 single handedly created the horror FPS with flashlights in the dark. It took atmosphere, graphics, and sound design to a whole new level, and the game STILL looks stunning TO THIS DAY.
